corpus: mybodycorpai apps/web @ 77a623b (99 files, 183 components) + the tool's own 820-test suite
method: Nine finder agents (analysis soundness, emitter correctness, false-pass hunting, CLI contract, docs truth, security, performance, test vacuity, DX) produced 45 raw findings, 43 after dedup. The verification fan-out died mid-run on an account spend limit, so every finding below was verified BY HAND with a concrete probe before being recorded — and findings that could not be reproduced are recorded as unverified rather than as defects.

severityAnchors.P0: emitted suite broken, silently passes, or lies; or the tool corrupts user files
severityAnchors.P1: wrong analysis output, docs claim contradicted by code, or a CI gap that lets P0s ship
severityAnchors.P2: performance, DX, error-message quality, design friction
severityAnchors.P3: opportunity aligned with the product's spirit

findings.title: An unknown task id was filtered away, so a typo ran zero tasks and exited 0
findings.claim: taskIds.map(findTask).filter(Boolean) discarded unknown ids silently. Probe: runCore({taskIds:['unit']}) returned exitCode 0 with results:[] — a green run that tested nothing, the exact outcome the project forbids.
findings.fix: runCore throws UsageError naming the unknown id(s) and listing the valid ones. tests/r7-honesty.test.ts pins both the throw and the message content.

findings.title: --nextjs without an entry positional crashed in the report line after every task had run
findings.claim: reproCommand read opts.pattern (typed string, genuinely undefined under Next.js auto-detection) instead of the resolved local. Probe: `bun src/bin.ts --nextjs <app> --ci --tasks perf-static` died with 'The "path" property must be of type string, got undefined' AFTER the work was done.
findings.fix: The resolved pattern is passed to reproCommand, and reproCommand renders a missing pattern as <entry> rather than throwing from path.relative. Pinned at unit level and by a real --nextjs-without-entry run that now completes and writes its own command line.

findings.title: --changed with a ref git cannot resolve reported 'nothing affected' and exited 0
findings.claim: changedFiles ran three git commands and skipped each nonzero exit with a bare `continue`, so a typo'd ref — or a ref absent from a shallow CI clone — produced an empty changed set and a green run for a comparison that never happened.
findings.fix: changedFiles verifies the checkout (`rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`) and then the ref (`rev-parse --verify <ref>^{commit}`), throwing a UsageError that distinguishes 'not a git checkout' from 'ref does not resolve here'. The FR-017 regression test now runs against a real one-commit repo so both invariants stay pinned.

findings.title: A file biome could not parse was reported clean by the a11y sweep
findings.claim: biome emits `parse` diagnostics for an unreadable file (a merge-conflict marker, unsupported syntax), and the sweep's category filter ('lint/a11y') dropped them, so the run reported 'a11y: 0 finding(s)' for a file it never analysed. biome's exit code was read and discarded.
findings.fix: Parse-failure diagnostics ride through the category filter as findings. A file the analyser could not read is never a pass. tests/r7-honesty.test.ts pins it with a merge-conflict fixture, plus a clean-file control proving the guard did not become noise.

findings.title: The emitted RSC spec's rendered-output assertion could not fail
findings.claim: `expect(document.body.innerHTML.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` holds no matter what the component rendered — @testing-library always appends its container div to document.body — so an RSC component that rendered nothing still passed its only output assertion.
findings.fix: The spec captures the render result and asserts on `rendered?.container.innerHTML.length ?? 0`, kept OUTSIDE the try so an assertion failure is reported as itself rather than swallowed by the guard catch. Executing the emitted artefact caught a scoping bug in the first attempt — the three execution tests are why.

findings.title: Skills and docs carried claims B-8/B-9 had already falsified
findings.claim: The flawless-react skill still listed z.infer aliases as unresolvable; flawless-unit-browser called zod inference 'a recorded frontier, not a bug' and presented the FR-027 async-cn stub as current; generated-suite.md said provider.tsx is 'written once and never overwritten' when --force regenerates it (the code comment at providerWrapper.ts:88 says so); README claimed 424 tests against a suite of 820.
findings.fix: All five claims corrected: the zod subset is described where the limits are stated, the cn wart is marked historical-and-fixed, the provider claim now separates the derived provider.tsx from the never-regenerated provider.fixtures.ts, and the README's test count is replaced with a phrasing that cannot drift.

reportedNotReproduced.title: Unescaped fetch() URL breaks out of the emitted describe() title
reportedNotReproduced.note: A component fetching a URL containing a double quote did not produce the claimed emission in a standalone unit-browser run (the fetch-spec path needs an --api spec). The escaping concern is real in principle; recorded for a targeted probe with apiRoutes present rather than claimed as a defect.

reportedNotReproduced.title: getAllBy* click trigger makes the skip-when-absent guard dead code
reportedNotReproduced.note: Same path as above — unreproduced without an API spec in the run. Kept as a candidate, not a finding.

reportedNotReproduced.title: Emitted e2e route specs pass while rendering the login screen
reportedNotReproduced.note: The generated global-setup is a documented hand-fill stub (the flawless-e2e-load skill's anti-vacuous probes exist for exactly this), so 'green by default' is the documented pre-fill state rather than a silent lie. Recorded as an opportunity — see backlog B-12 — not a defect.

reportedNotReproduced.title: foldLocals folds let/var; returnedExpression skips nested guards; named-import child re-export mismatch
reportedNotReproduced.note: Three analysis-soundness claims whose verification agents died before reproduction. Each needs a constructed component fixture to confirm or refute; carried into the next round's finder pass rather than recorded on unverified authority.
